title: Cron Syntax & Special Strings 📅
description: Master the five time fields, ranges, steps, and special shortcuts like @daily and @reboot.

slides.title: Beyond the Asterisk 🌟
slides.content:
## Fine‑Tuning Time

You can specify:
- Single value: `5`
- List: `1,3,5`
- Range: `1-5`
- Step: `*/15` (every 15 minutes)
- Combinations: `1-10,20-30`

These work in any time field.

slides.title: Examples in Action
slides.content:
Various schedules:
```
0 * * * *        # hourly at minute 0
0 0 * * *        # daily at midnight
0 0 * * 0        # weekly at midnight on Sunday
0 0 1 * *        # monthly on the 1st at midnight
0 0 1 1 *        # yearly on Jan 1st at midnight
*/10 * * * *     # every 10 minutes
0 8-18 * * *     # every hour from 8 AM to 6 PM
```

quizData.question: What does `*/5 * * * *` mean?
quizData.explanation: `*/5` in the minute field means every 5 minutes.

slides.title: Day of Week vs Day of Month 📆
slides.content:
## Watch the Logic

If you specify both day‑of‑month (3rd field) and day‑of‑week (5th field), the job runs when **either** condition is true (OR logic).

Example: `0 0 13 * 5` runs at midnight on the 13th of the month AND every Friday. To restrict to "Friday the 13th", you'd need a script that checks the date and only then executes.

slides.title: Restrict to Friday 13th
slides.content: The crontab would be `0 0 13 * 5 /script`, but the script itself checks if it's actually Friday (redundant). Better: `0 0 13 * 5 test $(date +%d) -eq 13 && /script`.

quizData.question: A cron job with both day‑of‑month and day‑of‑week set runs only when both are true.
quizData.explanation: They are OR'd, not AND'd. The job runs if either condition matches.

slides.title: Special Strings – Easy Shortcuts 🎁
slides.content:
## Instead of Five Numbers

Cron provides handy aliases:
- `@reboot`    – run once at startup.
- `@yearly`  / `@annually` – 0 0 1 1 *
- `@monthly` – 0 0 1 * *
- `@weekly`  – 0 0 * * 0
- `@daily`   / `@midnight` – 0 0 * * *
- `@hourly`  – 0 * * * *

Example: `@daily /usr/bin/backup.sh`

slides.title: Using @reboot
slides.content:
Run a script when the system starts:
```
@reboot /home/alice/start-services.sh
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Some cron daemons support second‑level resolution using a non‑standard seventh field. Stick to standard for portability.
